title: Burnley break transfer record to sign Robbie Brady and Ashley Westwood
trail: Burnley have completed the signing of Robbie Brady from Norwich and Ashley Westwood from Aston Villa, who have secured a deal for Brentford’s Scott Hogan
body: Burnley have completed the signing of the Republic of Ireland international Robbie Brady for a club record fee of around £13m. Sean Dyche had made the versatile 25-year-old his priority in the January market despite also agreeing a fee for Hull City’s Andrew Robertson and eventually got his man, with Brady signing a three-and-a-half-year deal. His arrival took Burnley’s spending on transfer deadline day to £18m after they completed the signing of Ashley Westwood from Aston Villa for an undisclosed fee, believed to be in the region of £5m. The 26-year-old has signed a three-and-a-half-year contract with the option of a further year. Westwood’s move brings to an end almost five years at Villa Park, during which he made 162 appearances for the club, – including 124 in the Premier League – and he could make his debut for Burnley when they travel to Watford on Saturday. “I’m delighted to be here,” Westwood said. “It’s happened fast but I’ve been made to feel very welcome and I can’t wait to get going. It feels like a proper football club and homely, and that’s what I like.” Meanwhile, Villa have won the race to sign Scott Hogan from Brentford after the striker’s mooted move to West Ham United failed to materialise. Slaven Bilic’s side had been the frontrunners to sign the 24-year-old, who once played for Stocksbridge Park Steels, the same non-league club who used to have Jamie Vardy on their books, but the club decided not to come back with a fourth bid having had three offers turned down by Brentford this month, one worth up to £12.5m. Brentford were holding out for a £15m fee including bonuses and it is understood that Villa were the first to come close to matching that despite interest from Crystal Palace and West Bromwich Albion, with an offer of £10m up front and an extra £5m due if certain clauses related to appearances and goals are met. Hogan’s previous club, Rochdale, are also owed 30% of the fee because of a sell‑on clause they negotiated when they sold the Salford-born striker in 2014. It caps a meteoric rise for Hogan, who was turned down by Rochdale twice before the club eventually signed him from non‑league Hyde United in 2013. However, his new club were beaten by his previous one on Tuesday night, Villa going down 0-3 at Brentford in the Championship. His arrival takes Villa’s spending this season to more than £70m, having also signed Henri Lansbury from Nottingham Forest and the Iceland international Birkir Bjarnason, among others.
